products.name: August Wi-Fi Smart Lock (4th Gen)
products.badge: Best retrofit for a phone-free exit
products.summary: A retrofit smart lock that clamps onto the inside of your existing single-cylinder deadbolt and keeps the outside keyhole and your key. Built-in Wi-Fi gives remote unlock, so a friend or your landlord can let you in from their phone if you are standing outside without keys.
products.renterNote: Replaces only the interior thumbturn side with a screwdriver install, and your existing keys still work. Caveat for lockouts: the keypad for phone-free codes is sold separately, it runs on two CR123 batteries, and owners report changing them every 3 to 7 months.
pros: Fits over most single-cylinder deadbolts from the inside, so the exterior and your key stay as they are
Built-in Wi-Fi (2.4 or 5 GHz) means remote unlock without a separate bridge
Auto-lock and DoorSense can re-lock the door, so you can also set up auto-unlock as you arrive
cons: Keypad for entering a code from outside is a separate purchase
Owners report battery changes every 3 to 7 months, which matters for a lockout-prevention lock

products.name: SwitchBot Lock Pro
products.badge: Best add-on keypad and fingerprint combo
products.summary: A battery-powered motor that mounts over your existing thumbturn and keeps the original lock and key. Pair it with the separate Keypad Touch and you can get in by fingerprint, passcode or NFC card without a phone.
products.renterNote: Mounts on the inside with brackets (SwitchBot also supplies adhesive and a door magnet), leaves the original lock and key in place, and Techlicious found it came off with no trace. The keypad and the hub for remote unlock are separate purchases, and fit depends on your lock, so check SwitchBot's compatibility list before you buy.
pros: Keeps your original lock and key, so the landlord's cylinder is untouched
Works with a separate Keypad Touch for fingerprint, passcode and NFC card entry
Low Battery Unlock keeps the lock working after the low-battery warning, per Techlicious
cons: Keypad and the hub for remote unlock are not included in the lock-only listing
Door fit varies; reviewers hit alignment and magnet-sensor problems on some doors

products.name: Yale Approach Lock with Wi-Fi and Keypad Touch
products.query: Yale Approach Lock Deadbolt Wi-Fi Keypad B-YRR110-F-WF1-N-BSP
products.summary: Yale's first retrofit smart lock installs over your existing deadbolt on the inside and ships with a biometric keypad and a Wi-Fi bridge. You can get in by fingerprint or code without a phone, and the key still works.
products.renterNote: The lock goes on the inside and you keep your keys; the included keypad can be stuck on with an adhesive pad or screwed on, so you can keep it drill-free. PCWorld found the install took more steps than a full-replacement deadbolt, and the lock's mounting plate screws through the existing latch into the exterior hardware.
pros: Keypad, fingerprint reader and Wi-Fi bridge are all included, so you can enter without a phone
Keeps your existing key as a backup
Keypad mounts with an included adhesive pad or screws and is IPX5 rated
cons: More install steps than a full-replacement deadbolt, and the bridge takes up an outlet within about 30 feet (PCWorld)
Owners report a 3-5 second fingerprint lag, power-cycling the bridge every six months or so, and no HomeKit

products.name: Master Lock Portable Key Lock Box 5400EC
products.query: Master Lock Portable Key Lock Box 5400EC
products.matchName: Master Lock Portable Key Lock Box
products.summary: A combination key box that hangs by its shackle over a door knob, so you can keep a spare key at your own door and open it with a code you set. It needs no power, no phone and no drilling, which is why it is the simplest lockout fix.
products.renterNote: Hangs over most ball, biscuit and tulip door knobs, so nothing is drilled or glued. Caveats: it is a theft deterrent, not a safe (owners report a burglar smashing one open), it shows from the hallway, and check your lease and landlord before leaving a key outside.
pros: Nothing to charge or replace: a resettable 4-digit combination
Holds up to 5 standard house keys, per Amazon listing
Vinyl-coated shackle hangs on a door knob without tools
cons: Not a safe: a verified buyer reported a burglar breaching one, and another reviewer says it only deters theft
A few owners report mechanism problems, such as a unit that would not open or accepted a wrong code
